name: Longer Ray7S
tagline: Enclosed Class 1 diode with Klipper firmware, sold in 7.5W, 15W, 20W and 40W versions
tldr: The Longer Ray7S, launched in October 2026, is an enclosed Class 1 diode laser running Klipper firmware with vibration compensation, 600 mm/s motion, Wi-Fi and a bed of about 305 × 305 mm. Longer sells four laser powers: 7.5W from $279.99, 15W at $369.99, 20W at $529.99 and 40W at $849.99, the only one with the air pump included (Basic Sets, Longer store, October 2026). Open a version for exact specs and benchmarks.
mainObjective: Enclosed engraving and cutting at home, with a power level for each budget

Klipper firmware with vibration compensation and 600 mm/s motion on every version
Four powers in the same cabinet, from a fine engraver to a 40W cutter with air pump included

New in October 2026: no independent reviews yet
beginnerNotes: This overview covers the whole Longer Ray7S line. Take the 7.5W or 15W if you mostly engrave, the 20W for mixed engraving and cutting, and the 40W if thick cuts are the main job. All four share the same Class 1 cabinet, Klipper firmware and software.
proTips: Route the exhaust outdoors even with the Class 1 cabinet. Add the air pump to any version below 40W if you plan to cut. Run a material test grid before production runs.
primaryUse: Enclosed Class 1 diode laser line with Klipper firmware for home engraving and cutting

editorialDepth.advantages: The Ray7S is Longer's budget answer to enclosed lasers like the xTool S1: a Class 1 cabinet, Klipper firmware and 600 mm/s motion for a fraction of the price. The real choice is the module: a fine engraver at 7.5W or 15W, an all-rounder at 20W, or a 40W cutter with the air pump included.
editorialDepth.limitations: Every version is a diode with a bed of about 305 × 305 mm: no clear acrylic, no large panels. The air pump is extra below 40W. Launched in October 2026, the Ray7S has no independent reviews of its cabinet, exhaust or reliability yet.

faq.question: Which Longer Ray7S should I buy?
faq.answer: The 7.5W ($279.99) or 15W ($369.99) if you mostly engrave; the 20W ($529.99) for regular cuts in 3–6 mm plywood; the 40W ($849.99) if thick cuts are the main job, and it is the only one with the air pump included. Prices are Basic Sets on Longer's store in October 2026.

faq.question: Is the Ray7S really Class 1?
faq.answer: Longer sells it as a Class 1 laser: with the lid closed, the cabinet contains the beam, so no glasses are needed to watch a job. That rating only holds with the lid shut.
